questions.question_text:
A flat roof has an area of $340\text{ m}^{2}$.
During a storm, $18$ mm of rain falls on it.
Find the volume of water that falls on the roof, in cubic metres.

options.why: Multiplied $340\times18$ without converting the depth from millimetres to metres, giving an answer $1000$ times too large.
Converted $18$ mm to $0.0018$ m, moving the decimal point four places instead of three.
Added the area and the depth instead of multiplying them.

questions.question_text:
A shed roof has an area of $96\text{ m}^{2}$.
If $35$ mm of rain falls on it, how many litres of water fall on the roof?

options.why: Stopped at the volume in cubic metres and labelled it litres, without multiplying by $1000$.
Converted cubic metres to litres by multiplying by $1\,000\,000$ instead of by $1000$.
Converted $35$ mm to $0.35$ m instead of $0.035$ m.

questions.question_text:
A rectangular warehouse roof measures $24$ m by $15$ m. During a storm $28$ mm of rain falls on it.
Find the volume of water that falls on the roof, in kilolitres.

options.why: Multiplied by $28$ without converting the depth from millimetres to metres.
Used the perimeter of the roof, $2(24+15)$, in place of its area.
Converted $28$ mm to $0.28$ m instead of $0.028$ m.

questions.question_text:
A site plan is drawn to a scale of $1:500$.
A rectangular roof measures $3$ cm by $2$ cm on the plan.
If $24$ mm of rain falls on the roof, find the volume of water collected, in litres.

options.why: Scaled the plan area of $6\text{ cm}^{2}$ by the linear factor $500$ instead of scaling each length, making the roof area $500$ times too small.
Stopped at the volume in cubic metres and labelled it litres.
Multiplied by $24$ without converting the depth from millimetres to metres.

questions.question_text:
A house roof has an area of $185\text{ m}^{2}$ and the average annual rainfall is $600$ mm, but $20\%$ of the rain is lost to overflow and leaks.
How much water is collected in a year, in kilolitres?

options.why: Found the total rainfall on the roof and ignored the $20\%$ that is lost.
Found the water lost, $20\%$ of the total, instead of the water collected.
Increased the total by $20\%$ instead of decreasing it by $20\%$.

questions.question_text:
During a storm, $45$ mm of rain falls on a roof of area $120\text{ m}^{2}$.
Only $85\%$ of it reaches the tank.
Find the volume of water that reaches the tank, in litres.

options.why: Found the total rainfall on the roof and ignored the fact that only $85\%$ reaches the tank.
Found the $15\%$ that is lost instead of the $85\%$ that reaches the tank.
Applied the $85\%$ correctly but left the answer in cubic metres and labelled it litres.

questions.question_text:
A house has a roof area of $225\text{ m}^{2}$ and the average annual rainfall is $800$ mm, of which $10\%$ is lost due to inefficient collection.
Town water costs $\$2.50$ per kilolitre.
How much could be saved in a year by using the collected tank water instead of town water?

options.why: Priced all $180\text{ kL}$ of rainfall without subtracting the $10\%$ lost.
Priced the $18\text{ kL}$ lost instead of the $162\text{ kL}$ collected.
Increased the rainfall volume by $10\%$ instead of decreasing it, then priced $198\text{ kL}$ at $\$2.50$ per kilolitre.

questions.question_text:
All the rain falling on a roof of area $180\text{ m}^{2}$ is piped into a rectangular tank whose base measures $2$ m by $1.5$ m.
During a storm $20$ mm of rain falls.
By how many centimetres does the water level in the tank rise?

options.why: Found the rise in metres but labelled it centimetres without multiplying by $100$.
Used the rainfall volume of $3.6\text{ m}^{3}$ as the rise in metres without dividing by the tank's base area.
Converted the rainfall depth of $20$ mm to centimetres and gave that instead of the rise in the tank.

questions.solution_text:
$20\text{ mm}=0.02\text{ m}$
$V=180\times0.02$
$=3.6\text{ m}^{3}$
$A_{\text{tank}}=2\times1.5$
$=3\text{ m}^{2}$
$\text{rise}=\dfrac{3.6}{3}$
$=1.2\text{ m}$
$=120\text{ cm}$
